name: Biscuits
instructions: Preheat to 450°. Combine dry ingredients in bowl and grate in cold butter. Combine with fork and add milk. Mix well and knead the dough about a dozen times. Flatten dough on counter to 3/4" and cut out rounds with a drinking glass. Bake 10-12 minutes from fresh, 15-18 minutes from frozen.
notes: Makes 8-10. Pioneer Woman recipe, May 2013. Can freeze unbaked rounds on a cookie sheet then transfer to freezer bag divided with parchment.

name: Sausage Gravy
instructions: Slice sausage into patties and cook in skillet, then set aside. Over low/medium heat combine the flour with sausage grease still in skillet. Whisk constantly for about 2 minutes until you get a deep brown color. Continue whisking and add in the milk, salt, and pepper. Allow to thicken over low heat, stirring occasionally. Add more milk if gravy gets too thick, more flour if it gets too thin. Serve hot with biscuits.

name: Cinnamon Rolls
instructions:
Place hot water, egg, butter, sugar, and salt in bread machine. Add 3 cups flour and make a small well in the flour and add yeast. Set bread machine to dough cycle for 90 minutes and start — go through the entire cycle.

When dough is ready, roll out on a floured surface. Spread softened butter over the surface. Sprinkle with 1/4-1/2c white sugar. Sprinkle with a lot of cinnamon — the surface of dough will look pretty brown. Roll into a log and shape to make even. Divide into 12 rolls. Place in greased 9x13 pan. Let rise to double, covered loosely with plastic wrap, about 20 minutes.

Preheat oven to 375°F. Bake 20-25 minutes until done. Frost with cream cheese frosting — add 1-2 drops maple extract for a kick. Can frost warm or cold.
notes: Makes 12 rolls in a 9x13 pan. September 2024.

name: Pancakes
ingredients: blueberries, strawberries, cinnamon, chocolate chips, or pecans (optional add-ins)
instructions: Combine milk and ACV in measuring cup and let sit while you melt the butter. Combine first four dry ingredients into mixing bowl plus any add-ins. Add eggs to milk mixture and beat with a fork, then add melted butter. Pour liquid into flour mix and stir. Spoon onto hot griddle (250°) and cook until dry around the edges before flipping — around 3 minutes per side, should be golden brown. Serve with butter and syrup.

name: Homemade Granola Cereal
instructions: Preheat 250°. Cover baking sheet with parchment paper. Melt butter with honey over low heat, remove from heat and stir in vanilla and salt. Mix first 8 dry ingredients together and pour honey mixture over everything, evenly coating. Spread evenly over pan and bake 75 minutes. Be careful not to burn. When done, cool on pan then break up into small chunks. Store in airtight container up to two weeks.

name: Crepes
instructions: Put everything in blender, blend and chill for at least 30 minutes. Heat 10-inch skillet to medium heat. Butter the pan once hot. Stir chilled batter and pour a scant 1/4c into skillet. Tip and swirl pan so batter covers the bottom. Cook to golden brown on bottom (about 1 minute) and gently flip with fingers. Cook another 30 seconds until golden brown. Stack on plate. Fill and fold with either sweet or savory fillings.

name: Bacon Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°. Slice the jalapeños lengthwise and seed them. Fill each half with cream cheese. Slice the bacon into thirds and either wrap or lay one piece atop each jalapeño half. Place jalapeños on a metal grate on top of a cookie sheet. Bake 25 minutes.

name: No-Bake Granola Bars
instructions: Stir everything together until well-mixed. Put wax or parchment paper in a casserole dish and spread mixture evenly. Store in fridge.

name: Applesauce (Crock Pot)
instructions: Chop apples, removing the cores. Mix everything in the crock pot and cook on high for 3-4 hours. When finished, mash with a potato masher to desired consistency. Store in jar in fridge. Easily doubled.

name: Palisade Peach Salad
ingredients: fresh basil leaves, chopped to taste
instructions: Toss peaches, salt, and honey together. Fold in basil, chevre, and lemon zest. Serve immediately.

name: Pork Chops
instructions: Coat the bottom of one skillet with olive oil and cook the pork on low to medium heat. Season with salt and pepper on both sides, flipping occasionally for an even cook. While the pork is cooking, chop the onion and apple and heat on low heat in a second skillet. After 5 minutes add applesauce or cider if desired. Once the pork is cooked through, add the veggie and fruit mix to the pork skillet, surrounding and atop the pork. Turn to low heat and cook 3-5 more minutes. Melt a thin slice of cheese on top, add mushrooms and cook a few more minutes. Serve with salad.

name: Refried Beans (Crock Pot)
ingredients: 2c pinto beans, soaked ~8 hours and rinsed
instructions:
Crock Pot: Combine all ingredients in crock pot and cook on high for 8 hours. Mash together into a coarse paste. Serve with shredded cheese and hot sauce, or with homemade corn tortillas.

Pressure Cooker variation: After beans have soaked, rinse and put in pressure cooker. Add chili pepper, cumin, garlic, and paprika. Add enough water so you can see it through the beans. Cook ~40 minutes on high pressure.

name: Beef Stew (Crock Pot)
instructions: Chop the meat, carrots, potatoes, and onion to desired sizes. Put everything in the crock pot and cook on high for 4 hours.

name: No Yeast Pizza Dough
instructions: Preheat oven to 415° — the longer the oven is hot the better. Mix all ingredients until dough is soft but not sticky. Knead for several minutes and roll out on parchment-lined cornmeal-sprinkled pizza pans. Shape crusts according to taste (thin, thick, or stuffed). Brush with a little olive oil and any extra desired seasonings like garlic. Top with desired toppings and bake 18-22 minutes until cheese is bubbling and browning and crust is brown. To store unbaked dough: coat dough ball with olive oil, wrap in plastic wrap, keep in fridge or freezer.

name: Etouffee
instructions: Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet and add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, and celery. Cook on medium heat 10-15 minutes until veggies are tender. While that is cooking, make the rice by boiling in water until water boils off. Mix the flour with water until smooth and add the mixture to the veggies, cooking 1-2 minutes. Add meat and cook on low for 10-15 minutes. Add seasonings and green onions and cook 5 more minutes. Serve over rice.
notes: Serves 8. From Christmas card from Xander. December 2014.

name: Lasagna (Crock Pot)
ingredients: mushrooms, onion, bell pepper to taste
oregano, sage, salt, pepper, thyme, basil to taste
instructions: Brown the meat, drain and stir in the water and crushed tomato. Add chopped mushrooms, onions, and peppers to taste plus seasonings (oregano, sage, salt, pepper, thyme, basil). Combine the ricotta, 1½-2c mozzarella, 2T parmesan, and the egg in a separate bowl. Layer the crock pot with meat sauce, noodles (broken to fit), and cheese mixture. Repeat layers. Add a final layer of meat sauce. Cook on low 4-6 hours until liquid is absorbed. Sprinkle with remaining mozzarella and parmesan and cook 10 more minutes covered.

name: Pulled Chicken (Crock Pot)
ingredients: 1 onion, peeled and cut in half
instructions: Place onion pieces in the bottom of crock pot and place chicken breasts on top. Mix all remaining ingredients together and pour over chicken — it's okay if some drips to the bottom. Cook on low for 7-8 hours. Shred with fork and serve with flatbread and rice or buns and pickles. A little hot sauce is great on it. Makes great leftovers served cold. Leftover chicken also works well in spaghetti, chili, soup, and stir-fry.

name: Black Bean Fiesta
ingredients: 1c black beans, drained (or 1 can — see notes)
instructions:
Put everything in a pan and stir-fry on med/high heat with a little hot sauce until warm. Serve with rice and flatbread. Tip: chop and freeze veggies ahead of time for a very quick supper.

For dried beans: put dried beans in pot with water and simmer slightly covered for 1-1½ hours. Can be prepared ahead of time, drained, and stored in fridge.
notes: Serves 4-8. Two cans of beans can be used but cooking from dry is much more budget-friendly. September 2016.

name: Macaroni and Cheese
instructions: Put large pot of water on high heat and bring to a boil. Once boiling add pasta and cook until desired tenderness. Meanwhile, melt butter in saucepan on medium/low heat. Add flour and mix. Stir in milk. Slowly add handfuls of shredded cheese while stirring, melting before adding more. Sauce will smell cheesy when you've added enough. After noodles are cooked, drain and return to pot. Stir cheese sauce in. Serve with pepper and hot sauce, garnish with any leftover cheese.

name: Pot Pie Soup
ingredients: paprika, salt, pepper, garlic powder to taste
2 cans chicken breast (Great Value Premium Chunk, 12.5oz)
frozen peas and carrots, or carrots chopped and cooked
instructions: Melt butter in large pot, stir in flour, all on low heat. Add milk. Add broth. Stir in chicken (do not drain). Stir in however much of the veggies you want. Turn up heat to medium-low. Serve with biscuits. Tip: can put the soup together while the oven preheats for biscuits and let it warm up while biscuits bake. Can also mix veggies together and freeze in single-serving bags for future use. If using leftover pulled chicken instead of canned, add 1c broth.
notes: Serves 6-8. From Elisabeth Watkins. January 2017. One of our quickest and favorite recipes.

name: Gumbo
instructions: Cook sausage in large skillet on medium heat. Once cooked, remove and cut up. Turn skillet back on with sausage fat still in it and cook onions on med/high heat until translucent, about 2 minutes — stir often. Add garlic and seasoning, stir until fragrant (30 sec). Add flour and stir to coat everything (~1 min). Add tomatoes, stirring occasionally until they release juices (~2 min). Remove skillet from burner, put a large pot in its place, and dump everything from skillet into pot. Add broth, sausage, and okra. Simmer until ready to serve and okra is thawed. Serve over rice.

name: Stuffed Peppers (Crock Pot)
instructions: Brown beef. Stir in everything else and simmer while you cut the tops off and remove seeds from peppers. If peppers are already prepared, no need to simmer. Stuff peppers and replace tops. Cook on low in crock pot with a little olive oil in the bottom so peppers don't burn, 3-4 hours.

name: Chicken Stuffing Casserole (Crock Pot)
ingredients: sage, salt, pepper, rosemary to taste
instructions: Mix together cornbread, onion, and celery. Put chicken in crock pot and season. Put cheese on top of chicken (if using) and top with cornbread, onion, and celery mixture. Mix together the soup, sour cream, and water and put mixture on top of stuffing. Cook on low 4 hours, 6 hours if from frozen.

name: Cornflake Chicken
instructions: Preheat to 400° and grease baking dishes with olive oil. Crush the cornflakes (use a wine bottle while they're in the mixing bowl) and add all the seasonings. Quarter the chicken breasts (slicing long-ways through the middle first) and dip in the milk. Put milky meat into cornflake mixture and coat on all sides. Bake 45-60 minutes, twice using a spatula to lift up and flip chicken to ensure it won't burn on the bottom.

name: Leftover Chili (Crock Pot)
instructions: Put everything in the crock pot and cook on low 6-8 hours. Serve with Fritos and cheese.
notes: Serves 6-8. November 2011. Great use of leftover pulled chicken and beans.

name: Falafel
ingredients: 1c dried chickpeas, cooked — OR — 2 cans chickpeas, drained
cumin, paprika, salt, pepper to taste
instructions: Puree chickpeas in food processor or blender or smash with a potato masher — it's okay if not all of them smash up. Mix in remaining ingredients, adding more water if too crumbly and more flour if too sticky. Form into patties and put in skillet with hot olive oil. Cook until looking dry and flip — bottom side will be golden brown. Cook other side until golden brown as well. Add more oil if needed. Serve with sliced tomatoes and onion, homemade ranch, hot sauce, and flatbread.

name: Chicken Noodle Soup
instructions: In large pot on medium-high heat sauté carrots, celery, and onion in olive oil until they soften (~7 minutes). Add garlic and sauté another 2 minutes. Add broth and spices and bring to a boil, simmer for 5 minutes. Add noodles and boil for ~10 minutes (if needed add 1-2c water and more salt). Add chicken and boil 1-2 more minutes.

name: Maki Rolls
instructions:
Cook rice in water until completely absorbed, ~15 minutes. While cooking, on medium heat combine ACV, sugar and salt until dissolved. Place in small dish and cool in fridge until rice is done. Once rice is done remove from heat and stir in vinegar mixture with a fork. Let sit while you prep veggies.

Use a thick dish towel folded into a rectangle and topped with plastic wrap. Place a piece of Nori on top of plastic. Dip hands in water and put a thin layer of rice on top of Nori, leaving about 1/2 inch clear on top and bottom. Place veggies and fish on the end closest to you. Start rolling on the edge closest to you, using the wrap and towel to mold and compress. Slice into 8 pieces. Serve immediately with soy sauce and wasabi.
notes: Serves 2-4. September 2018. Can substitute other veggies.

name: Garden Veggie Chicken Skillet
ingredients: 3-5 medium potatoes, any variety, cut into small pieces
1 lb uncooked chicken breast, cut into small pieces
4c chopped veggies (zucchini, asparagus, mushrooms, onions, peppers)
instructions: Combine all ingredients in large skillet and stir dressing around to coat everything. Cover and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until veggies are tender and meat is cooked. Can serve over rice or pasta.

name: Yummy Wahoo Muffins (Beef and Cornbread)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°. Place parchment paper cups in muffin tin. Brown beef and onion together, add remaining beef ingredients and allow to simmer in skillet for a few minutes. Meanwhile stir together dry muffin ingredients, add wet ingredients and stir until just mixed. Fill muffin cups 1/2 full with muffin batter. Spoon about a tablespoon of beef mix on top of each muffin cup. Bake 20 minutes. Serve with butter.
notes: Makes 12 muffins. February 2019. Named by Faith. Easy to double, or just double the beef recipe for more meat. Quadruple beef recipe for sloppy joes. Freezes well. Same heat and time works for just muffins or a 9x9 pan.

name: Lime Chicken (Crock Pot)
instructions: Pour mixture over chicken and cook in crock pot on low 7-8 hours or high 3-4 hours. Shred and serve in tacos or other dishes.

name: Sweet and Sour Chicken Legs
instructions: Preheat 350°. Put chicken in 9x13 baking dish. Mix remaining ingredients in small saucepan and heat briefly to melt honey and make sure it is well combined. Pour mixture over chicken. Cover and bake 45 minutes. Turn chicken over in sauce, cover, cook 15 more minutes.

name: Chicken Pot Pie
instructions: Preheat 350°. Boil broth, carrots, peas, potatoes, chicken, salt and pepper until veggies are tender. Mix cornstarch with cold water until smooth, stir mixture into broth/veggies and cook another minute to help thicken. Pour contents into 9x13 baking dish. In separate bowl stir together milk, mayo, and flour then spread mixture over veggies in baking dish. Bake 45 minutes until crust is golden brown.

name: Chicken and Spinach Zesty Soup
instructions: In large pot, cook onion, garlic, carrots, and red pepper in olive oil 3-5 minutes. Pour in broth and bring to boil. Add orzo and cook until tender. Stir in chicken, spinach, cream, lemon juice, salt, and dill and simmer until ready to serve.

name: Pressure Cooker Chicken and Stock
instructions: Season each chicken breast to taste. In Instant Pot put olive oil in pot and use sauté feature. Once hot (about 2 min) brown each chicken about 2 minutes on each side. After chicken is done browning, brown garlic. Pour in a small amount of water and scrape bottom of pot with a wooden spatula. Turn off pot, add the rest of the water, put trivet in and place chicken on top of trivet all three side by side like books. Close and seal lid, use pressure cook on high for 20 minutes. Allow to vent naturally. Chicken can be eaten as is or shredded for other recipes. Save stock in jar in fridge.

name: Chinese Hamburger Casserole
instructions: Preheat 350°. Brown the meat, add everything else except the noodles. Stir well and put in a 2-quart casserole dish. Cover and bake 30 minutes. Uncover and bake 30 more minutes. Sprinkle noodles on top and bake 15 more minutes.

name: Baked Potatoes
instructions:
Preheat to 450°. Wash potatoes and poke with fork all over. Bake 25 minutes on a drying rack. Brush with olive oil and turn potatoes over. Sprinkle with salt and bake another 25 minutes. Will be soft to squeeze. Serve immediately.

Alternate method: brush with oil, sprinkle with salt, wrap in foil and bake ~1 hour. Saves on cleanup.

name: Githeri
ingredients: 1/2t curry powder (or garlic, fennel, coriander, cumin, turmeric)
instructions: Sauté onions in large pan in olive oil. Stir in garlic, paprika, and curry powder. Low heat for ~1 minute. Add tomatoes and cook ~3 minutes. Add beans, corn, and veg stock, cover and simmer ~8 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add cilantro to top before serving. Can put in crock pot for easy reheat/potluck. Serve with Ugali.
notes: Serves 6-8. July 2022. Taken to potluck at FFBC.

name: Poor Man's Dismantled Pantry Sushi
ingredients: sesame seeds or Everything Bagel seasoning
instructions: Cook rice and let cool. Combine tuna with mayo and soy sauce. Sprinkle in seeds/seasoning. Stir/fold vinegar into rice. Scoop rice into small balls (use an ice cream scoop) onto plate. Top each with a small amount of tuna mix and cucumber, and sprinkle with more seeds.

name: Fresh Garden Chili
instructions: Sauté onions in butter in a large pot/skillet/pressure cooker, add beef and garlic and brown. Add remaining ingredients and simmer at least an hour. Alternatively put it all in the crock pot and cook on low the day you're going to serve it.
notes: Fall 2023. Taken to potluck chili contest.

name: Stir Fry Salad
ingredients: seasonings to taste (salt, pepper, ginger, paprika, crushed red pepper, basil, oregano, garlic, thyme, rosemary)
instructions: Chop, drain, and mix everything together. Freeze in quart-sized bags for later use. From freezer, heat in skillet with olive oil and include any seasonings you like. Serve with any meal that needs veggies, or over rice as its own meal.
notes: Serves 4-6. Great meal prep — freeze in portions for quick use.

name: Cauliflower Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 1 small head cauliflower (about 2 1/4 lbs), core removed and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
instructions: In a large skillet combine the cauliflower with the salt and 1 1/2T of the butter cut into small chunks. Pour in enough water to reach just below the top of the cauliflower pieces, cover and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer covered until cauliflower is tender, about 10 minutes. Transfer cauliflower with a slotted spoon to a bowl and bring liquid remaining in pan back to a boil. Boil liquid until reduced to about 1/3-1/2 cup. Working in two batches, transfer half of the cooked cauliflower to a blender and add half of the reduced liquid. Puree until smooth, scraping down sides as necessary. Transfer mixture to the skillet. Repeat with remaining cauliflower and liquid and heat the puree in the skillet, stirring, just until hot. Add salt to taste and serve, topping each portion with a tiny slice of the remaining 1 1/2T butter and a sprinkling of chives.
notes: Serves 6. Start to finish 55 minutes (25 minutes hands-on). Puree can be made ahead and heated in a double boiler or microwave.

name: Ranch Dressing
instructions: Stir everything together. Store in airtight container in fridge for up to 10 days. Serve on whatever.

name: All-Purpose Creole and Chili Seasoning
instructions: Mix everything together and store in a jar. Use for all sorts of things.
notes: December 2014. Referenced by many other recipes in the collection.

name: Grilled Chicken Dry Rub
instructions: Combine all dry ingredients with olive oil and coat chicken. Marinate for several hours or longer. Grill on medium-high heat until chicken is cooked through.

name: Italian Dressing
instructions: Mix dry seasonings together and store in a jar. To make dressing: combine 2T dry mix + 1/4c red wine vinegar + 2t water + 1/2c olive oil. Combine and serve.
notes: Makes ~1 1/2c dressing. February 2019. Store the dry mix in a jar and mix fresh dressing as needed.

name: Worcestershire Sauce
instructions: Bring all ingredients to a boil, stirring constantly. Simmer 1 minute. Cool. Store in fridge.

name: Flat Bread
instructions: Melt butter in small saucepan. Combine flour and salt in mixing bowl. Mix melted butter and water (or milk) into flour mixture until you have a ball of dough — start by stirring then mix by hand. Divide dough into two sections, then each section into 8 pieces while oil is heating on medium-high in the skillets. Roll out each piece into a thin circle and place in hot oil. Cook on each side 45 seconds to a minute. Store on plate wrapped in plastic wrap. Put more oil down after first 8 pieces.

name: Pumpkin Muffins
instructions: Preheat 325° and line muffin cups with parchment liners. Mix oil and honey with a whisk. Add eggs. Add pumpkin and milk. Add baking soda through cloves. Stir in flour and oats. Fill cups 3/4 full. Sprinkle tops with additional oats and cinnamon. Bake 22-25 minutes — toothpick will come out clean. Let cool before serving.
notes: Makes 12. October 2015. Used for Rainn's smash cake and worked well.

name: Blueberry Muffins
ingredients: 1c blueberries tossed with 1t whole wheat flour
instructions: Preheat 350°. In large bowl combine dry ingredients. In another bowl beat with whisk the oil and honey. Add the eggs and whisk. Add yogurt and vanilla and whisk. Pour onto dry mix and combine with spoon. Toss blueberries and flour together and fold into batter. Put into muffin cups (use parchment paper liners) and sprinkle tops with raw sugar. Bake 20-22 minutes. Cool completely.

name: Cornbread
ingredients: 2T butter or bacon grease for skillet
instructions: Preheat 450°. In large measuring cup measure out ACV and add milk to equal 1 1/2c of liquid. In large bowl whisk together the first four dry ingredients. Melt 2T of butter (or grease) in a 12" cast iron skillet on medium heat. Meanwhile add the egg and baking soda to the milk mixture and whisk. Add wet ingredients to dry and incorporate well but don't over-mix — batter will be lumpy. When the skillet is hot, add 1/4c of melted butter to batter while stirring, then immediately pour batter into skillet. Cook 1 minute, then place skillet in oven and bake 20 minutes.

name: Round Loaf Whole Wheat Bread (Pressure Cooker Rise)
instructions:
Put yeast in water and let sit ~3 minutes until it bubbles/foams. Mix dry ingredients together. Add water mixture and stir until just mixed — will be sticky and messy looking. Set in glass bowl in Instant Pot (no pot insert), cover with a pot lid (not original lid), and allow to rise 3 1/2 hours on yogurt setting.

Preheat oven to 450° and have a dutch oven (or pie dish with cake pan for a lid) heat up with the oven. Turn dough onto floured counter and gently shape into a ball. Brush with olive oil and sprinkle seasonings to taste. Put parchment paper in bottom of hot pie dish, gently place ball of dough in dish and cover with cake pan. Bake 30 minutes. Remove cake pan and bake 15 more minutes. Let cool before slicing.

name: Sandwich Bread
instructions: Sprinkle yeast on top of warm water and set aside. Combine salt with 2c flour. Blend in on medium speed the butter, honey, and yeast water for ~3 minutes. Stir in 1 1/4-1 3/4c flour until dough cleanly pulls away from the sides of the bowl. Knead on floured surface, adding 1/2-3/4c flour, until dough is smooth and elastic, ~10 minutes. Place dough in large oiled bowl, covered loosely, to rise ~30-45 minutes in a warm place (should double in size). Oil a standard loaf pan, punch down the dough and shape into loaf. Allow to rise in pan, loosely covered, 30-45 minutes (should double again). Bake at 350° for 40-45 minutes. Will sound hollow when tapped.

name: Communion Bread
instructions: Preheat 475°. Knead together, adding more flour or water as necessary. Roll as thin as you can. Set on parchment lined cookie sheet. Bake 4 minutes. Let cool and store in airtight container.

name: Ugali
instructions: Bring water to a boil. Slowly stir in cornmeal. Mixture will be very thick and firm. When it pulls away from the bottom of the pan and has the aroma of corn it's done, ~5 minutes. Put on large plate and shape into a ball. Can store in fridge ~3 days, reheat with a little water.

name: Bread Machine Bread
instructions: Place hot water, egg, butter, sugar, and salt in bread machine. Add 3 cups flour. Make a small well in the flour and add yeast. Set bread machine to dough cycle for 90 minutes (1 hour 30 minutes) and start. When dough is finished, pour directly into a greased bread pan. If needed, gently turn the bread or tuck in the edges so the top is smooth (it's okay if it is sticky). Place bread in COLD oven and set oven to 350°. Set timer for 30 minutes. When finished baking, remove from oven and carefully remove bread from the pan.
notes: Makes 12 slices. September/October 2025. By Erica Walker, rated 4.93/5 from 162 votes.

name: Zucchini Bread or Muffins
instructions: Preheat 350°. Grease loaf pan. Stir together zucchini through vanilla. Add dry ingredients and stir. Add nuts and raisins and fold in. Bake 55 minutes.
notes: 2024. Can also be made as muffins.

name: Chocolate Chip Skillet Cookies
instructions:
Preheat to 375°. Beat together butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla until smooth. Add flour, salt, and baking soda and beat until mixed. Stir in or beat in the chocolate chips.

For skillet cookies: shape the dough into a ball and divide into 8 parts. Flatten into cookie shape and bake in skillet 18-20 minutes. Center will be slightly doughy. Can also make 10" by dividing into four parts.

For regular cookies: shape dough into balls and bake 9-12 minutes.

Dough freezes great — bake from frozen at 8 minutes any time. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

name: Chocolate Pudding
instructions: Combine the first five ingredients in the pan and bring to boil over medium heat. Boil and stir for 2 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in last two ingredients (butter and vanilla). Divide into individual dishes, cover with plastic wrap on the surface. Chill.

name: Pie Crust
instructions: Grease the pie dish with a small amount of oil. Combine the dry ingredients with the coconut oil until you have good-looking crumbs. Slowly add cold water until you have a pliable ball of dough (not sticky but not crumbly). Roll out the dough on wax paper until desired size. Flip the dough into your pie dish using the wax paper. Remove the wax paper and shape your crust, trimming off excess dough. Use excess dough for a second pie or to make a covered pie. If pre-baking: 450° for 10 minutes.
notes: February 2015. Makes enough for one pie with extra for a covered pie.

name: Apple Pie
ingredients: pie crust (see recipe, makes top and bottom)
instructions: Preheat to 425°. Peel and slice apples and put in bowl. Add all dry ingredients and stir until apples are evenly coated. Place into unbaked pie crust and dot with butter. Place second pie crust on top and pinch edges together, trimming off any excess dough. Slit the top crust to allow steam. Cover edges with aluminum foil to prevent burning. Bake 45 minutes until filling bubbles through slits and crust is brown. Note: when baking with a crumb top, only bake 35-40 minutes.

name: Brownies
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Melt the butter in the pan and stir in all other ingredients until well-mixed. Add chocolate chips if desired. Pour into greased 9x9 dish. Bake 20-25 minutes.
notes: Serves 16. October 2015. Can be doubled for a 9x13 dish.

name: Molten Lava Cakes
instructions: Preheat to 450° and line muffin tin with parchment liners. Melt butter and chocolate together on low heat. Cool slightly while whisking together eggs, yolks, and sugar. Stir in chocolate mixture. Divide among 10 muffin cups and bake 6-8 minutes. Cakes will be puffed up but still jiggly in center. Turn upside down onto a plate, garnish with powdered sugar and strawberries and serve immediately.
notes: Serves 5 at 2 each. Makes 10. First made for game night. February 2017.

name: Orange Juice Yogurt
instructions: Put a spoonful of frozen OJ concentrate at the bottom of a cup or bowl. Add yogurt on top. Stir and enjoy. For a group: 3T OJ concentrate to 3/4c yogurt.

name: Peanut Butter Dreams
instructions:
Preheat 375°. In large bowl beat sugar, butter, and 1/4c peanut butter until light and fluffy. Beat in vanilla and eggs. Stir in flour, cocoa, and baking soda.

For filling: combine powdered sugar and 3/4c peanut butter.

Divide dough and filling into 24 parts each. Shape approximately 1T of dough around 1-inch peanut butter balls and cover completely. Place on parchment-lined cookie sheet and flatten with a glass. Bake 7-9 minutes. Should be set and slightly cracked.

name: Pumpkin Pie
instructions: Preheat 375°. Stir everything together and pour into pie shell until almost full. Cover edges of crust with foil. Bake 55-60 minutes. Cool before serving. Leftover filling can be used for mini pies, muffins, etc.

name: Banana Pudding
instructions: Combine milk, flour, vanilla, sugar, and eggs in saucepan over medium heat until it thickens, stirring often. In a casserole dish layer wafers, sliced bananas, and sauce, repeating until you run out of sauce and topping with wafers.

name: Cheesecake
instructions: Preheat 325°. Line pie pan/dish with parchment paper. Combine graham crackers and butter and press onto bottom of pie dish. Beat cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla. Add eggs and mix on low until just blended. Pour over the crust. Bake 50-55 minutes until center is almost set. Loosen parchment from edges of cake, refrigerate at least 4 hours.

name: Oatmeal Cookies
instructions: Preheat 375°. Beat butter through vanilla. Add egg and beat. Add flour, oats, and cinnamon and beat. If adding add-ins, beat in OJ and add-ins. Bake 8 minutes, flatten once removed from oven. If baking from frozen, bake 10 minutes.

name: Thumbprint Cookies
instructions: Preheat 375°, line cookie sheet with parchment. Beat butter and sugar, beat in vanilla and yolks, beat in flour and salt. Form into 1-inch balls, flatten slightly to leave small indentation in center. If baking fresh: 7 minutes. From frozen: 8 minutes, until bottoms are barely golden. Remove from oven and further define the indentations if needed. Fill each with approximately 1/2t of jam. Bake 4-5 more minutes until jam melts slightly and edges of cookie are lightly golden. Cool and serve.

name: Hidden Kiss Cookies
instructions: Preheat 375°. Beat butter, sugar, and vanilla. Add flour and nuts. Divide dough and shape each part around 8-10 chocolate chips (keeping them grouped together to substitute for Hershey kisses) and form into a ball. Bake 10 minutes fresh, 12 minutes from frozen. Cool completely and dip in powdered sugar.

name: Carrot Cupcakes
instructions:
Preheat to 350°. Combine first six dry ingredients in large bowl. Combine carrots and oil in small bowl, add to flour mixture until just mixed. Beat eggs in small bowl and add to everything else, stirring until just mixed. Line muffin tin with parchment cups, fill each 2/3 of the way. Bake 15 minutes until golden brown with springy tops. Cool.

Frosting: Beat cream cheese, butter, and vanilla until smooth. Slowly beat in powdered sugar until smooth. Put in small ziplock sandwich bag, cut off corner, and frost when cupcakes are cooled.

name: Baked Donuts
instructions: Mix but don't overmix ingredients. Fill donut pans about 3/4 full. Bake at 350° for about 20 minutes. After cooled, dust with sugar and cinnamon.

name: Custard Pie
instructions: Preheat 400°. In large bowl whisk eggs, then whisk in everything else. Pour into crust. Bake 30 minutes until knife comes out clean. Cool at room temperature, then move to fridge. Serve chilled.

name: Chocolate Milkshakes
instructions: Set ice cream on counter to slightly soften. In small saucepan heat 2T milk, sugar, and cocoa until well mixed. Remove from heat and cool at room temperature. Put 1/3c milk in blender, add ice cream, add chocolate mixture. Blend to desired consistency. Top with whipped cream. Can make any flavor — use less milk for fruity shakes.

name: Peanut Butter Cookies
instructions: Preheat 350°. Mix butter, sugar, syrup, peanut butter, eggs, and vanilla until well-mixed and fluffy. Add dry ingredients and mix until just combined. Measure out tablespoon-sized balls, push slightly flat with a fork. Bake 10 minutes. Allow to cool 5 minutes on baking sheet before transferring to wire rack.

name: Peach Pie
ingredients: 6-7 peaches, peeled and cut into chunks (not sliced)
crumb topping with cinnamon and pecans added (see recipe)
instructions: Combine all filling ingredients and set aside. Preheat 400°. Put pie dough in preheating oven with pie weights and pie shield. Once preheated, remove pie shell (keep shield on) and spoon peach mixture into shell. Top with crumb topping for fruit pies with cinnamon and pecans added to taste (prep this while preheating). Put pie on baking sheet and bake 20 minutes. Reduce heat to 375° and bake an additional 35 minutes. Peach juices will be bubbling and crumble will be browned. Cool 3 hours at room temperature.

name: Creamy Blueberry Pie
ingredients: 3c blueberries, fresh or frozen (if frozen thaw and drain)
instructions: Preheat 350°. Place berries in prepared pie shell and set aside. Combine sugar, flour, and salt. Add eggs and yogurt and whisk well. Pour mixture over blueberries. Top with crumb topping. Bake 50-55 minutes. Cool on wire rack.

name: Crumb Topping for Fruit Pies
instructions: Grate cold butter into large bowl. Add sugar and flour and mix with forks or pastry cutter until you have coarse crumbs. Keep extra in freezer. Can adjust portion as needed.
notes: April 2021. Used with Peach Pie and Creamy Blueberry Pie.

name: Whipped Cream
ingredients: 3T raw sugar (or 1/2T for less sweet version)
instructions: Chill your beaters and bowl in the freezer for at least 10 minutes. Beat cream and sugar on high for 2 minutes. Add the vanilla and continue beating on high for another 1-2 minutes until you have stiff peaks. Can also use honey or syrup, or less sugar. Best served immediately but can store in fridge 24-48 hours.
notes: The less sweet version (1/2T sugar, 1/4t vanilla) is still delicious — they think it is perfect.

name: Salted Caramel Sauce
ingredients: 1/2 stick butter (1/4c or 4T), cut in small pieces
instructions: In large saucepan stir sugar and water on medium-high until sugar is dissolved. Once dissolved, stop stirring and allow to boil 5-7 minutes until it begins smelling like caramel and color deepens. While boiling, heat the cream on low in a small saucepan. Reduce sugar heat to medium and stir in warmed cream — may bubble up, that's okay. Remove from heat and stir in butter until melted and smooth. Stir in vanilla and salt. Cool to room temperature. Store in jar in fridge up to one month.

name: Eggnog
instructions: In bowl, beat yolks until lighter in color, then slowly add sugar and beat until fluffy. Slowly heat milk, cloves, and cinnamon in saucepan until steamy hot — don't allow to boil. Temper the eggs by slowly adding half of the hot milk mix into the eggs, whisking constantly. Pour all of the mixture back into the saucepan. Cook on medium heat, stirring constantly — it will begin to thicken; remove from heat once it coats the wooden spoon. Stir in the cream. Let cool for one hour in the jar, partially covered. Add vanilla and nutmeg, close jar and shake vigorously. Chill 4-6 hours. Shake before serving.

name: Christmas French Toast
ingredients: bread of choice, cut 1 inch diagonally (G.H. raisin and walnut recommended)
instructions: Combine cream, eggs, vanilla, salt, cinnamon, and ground coffee in bowl. Dip the bread in the mix and place in a single layer in baking dishes. Chill 12-36 hours. Heat coconut oil in the skillet and brown the bread on both sides. Serve with bacon or sausage.
notes: Family recipe. Great for overnight prep.

name: Sweet Potatoes
ingredients: 2 medium to large yams, cooked, peeled, and diced
instructions: Preheat 350°. Mix first six ingredients and put in square casserole. For the topping, melt butter and syrup in small saucepan and stir into flour and pecans. Spread topping on top of potatoes and bake until bubbly, 25-30 minutes.

name: Green Bean Casserole
ingredients: 1 can cream of mushroom soup (Pacific brand is clean)
French fried onions (Sprouts gluten-free are clean)
instructions: Preheat 350°. Combine first four ingredients in large casserole. Stir in green beans and half of the onions. Bake 25 minutes. Stir, top with remaining onions, and bake 5 more minutes.
notes: Serves 4-6. November 2011. From Grandma Peggy. A Thanksgiving and Christmas tradition.

name: Thanksgiving Turkey (Crock Pot)
ingredients: salt, pepper, sage, thyme, marjoram to taste
potatoes, carrots, celery, onion, chopped and seasoned (optional)
instructions: Rinse turkey and pat dry. Rub with olive oil and seasonings and put in fridge for 24 hours. When ready to cook, put chicken stock in bottom of crock pot. Put lemon and garlic in cavity of turkey, or stuffing. Make sure crock pot lid is sealed — use foil and a belt if necessary. Cook on high 2 hours then low 4-6 hours, or just low for 8-12 hours. Optional: put chopped potatoes, carrots, celery, and onion on bottom of crock pot and around turkey — season first.

name: Hot Chocolate
instructions: In small saucepan over medium/low heat combine dry ingredients with about 2T of the milk until sugar and cocoa are dissolved. Add the rest of the milk and turn heat up to medium. Heat until hot and steamy, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat and stir in vanilla. Serve with whipped cream, marshmallows, cinnamon, peppermint, or chocolate chips — or plain. Easy to multiply. If you get up to a quart of milk use 1/4t salt.
notes: Serves 1. December 2017. Pro tip: make before a cold day and put in crock pot on keep warm until ready to drink.

name: Horchata
ingredients: 1 cup uncooked long grain white rice
1 Mexican cinnamon stick broken in half — or ground cinnamon when sticks unavailable
instructions: Rinse the rice under running water until the water runs clear. Add the rinsed rice, almonds, cinnamon stick, and 3 cups of water to a large bowl or pitcher. Cover and let it sit in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours, up to 24 hours. Pour the bowl of ingredients into a large blender and add the remaining 3 cups of water. Blend on high until completely smooth, about 2-5 minutes — work in batches if needed. Strain the blended mixture through a fine mesh strainer or nut milk bag to remove solids, straining 2-4 times to remove all grittiness. Pour into a large pitcher and mix in the milk, evaporated milk, sugar, and vanilla extract. Stir until all ingredients are well combined. Serve over ice and top with ground cinnamon.
notes: Serves 8. December 2024 — after watching Psych again. By Isabel Orozco-Moore, rated 4.79/5 from 56 votes. Dairy-free: use milk alternative. Nut-free: omit almonds. For sweeter version: replace sugar with 6-12oz sweetened condensed milk.

name: Copycat Takeout Egg Rolls
ingredients: 16 cups Taiwanese, green, or savoy cabbage, shredded
2 cups celery, shredded or finely chopped
2 tablespoons peanut, vegetable, or canola oil (plus more for frying)
3 cups roast pork, shredded or diced
instructions:
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Put the cabbage, carrots, and celery into the boiling water and cook about 2 minutes. Transfer to an ice bath and drain. Thoroughly squeeze out all excess water from the vegetables — this is critical, wet filling = soggy egg rolls.

Transfer dry veggies to a large mixing bowl. Add scallions, salt, sugar, sesame oil, 2T oil, five spice powder (if using), white pepper, roast pork, and cooked shrimp (if using). Toss together. Filling is ready to wrap.

To wrap: take a small fistful of filling, squeeze it a little in your hand until compressed, place on wrapper. Wrap like a burrito. Add a thin layer of beaten egg to seal. Line up on a lightly floured surface.

Heat oil to 325°F in a small pot — just enough to submerge the egg rolls. Fry a couple at a time for about 5 minutes until golden brown, keeping them moving so they fry evenly. Cool slightly and serve. Freeze leftovers in freezer bags and reheat in oven at 350°F until crispy.
notes: Makes about 24. 4.92/5 from 182 votes. By Bill.

name: Hot Bananas with Cinnamon Coconut Sauce
instructions:
Remove ends from bananas. Place bananas in a covered bamboo steamer over a pan of boiling water. Cook 5 minutes. Using tongs and a knife, peel off banana skins.

Combine flour, sugar, and cinnamon in a saucepan. Add coconut milk and stir until smooth. Cook, stirring, over medium heat until mixture boils and thickens, then simmer 2 minutes more. Serve sauce over hot bananas.
notes: Serves 4. Ready in under 30 minutes. From CDKitchen.

name: Wild Turkey with Cornbread Dressing
ingredients: turkey neck, liver, gizzards, and hearts (giblets)
3c other bread crumbs (biscuits, rolls, bread heels)
4 packages dry turkey gravy mix (for gravy)
instructions:
CORNBREAD: Grease a large cast iron skillet with solid shortening. Place in oven just above middle. Turn oven to 425°. While oven and skillet heat, combine cornmeal, flour, salt, and baking powder. In a 1-qt measure, combine milk, eggs, and oil. Make a well in dry ingredients, add liquids all at once and stir with a whisk until well combined. Pour batter into hot skillet and bake 30 minutes. Turn out and cool completely. Crumble into crouton-sized pieces. Store sealed until ready to use.

GIBLETS: Place necks, livers, gizzards, and hearts in a large pot with water. Sprinkle with salt. Bring to a boil, reduce to simmer, cover. Cook until very tender, about 1 hour. Remove giblets and chop into small pieces. Save broth.

DRESSING: Toss crumbled cornbread, 3c bread crumbs, chopped onion, sliced celery, salt, chopped boiled eggs, pepper, poultry seasoning, sage, and chopped giblets together in a large container. Add melted butter and 4c hot broth. Toss just enough to evenly distribute — don't overmix. Consistency should be a bit looser than the finished product. Add more broth if needed.

Spray a large deep pan with cooking spray. Cover bottom with a good layer of dressing. Dry turkey pieces and place on top — turkey should not touch the pan. Cover turkey well with dressing to within an inch of pan rim. Cover tightly with lid or heavy duty foil. Bake at 350° for 3 hours. Uncover and bake 30 more minutes. Put extra dressing in a greased casserole, cover, refrigerate until ready — bake at 350° for 1 hour, remove lid and bake 15 more minutes.

GRAVY: Prepare 4 packages dry turkey gravy mix using remaining turkey broth plus enough water to make 1 qt, per package directions.
notes: Classic family Thanksgiving recipe. Thaw turkey Tuesday night in refrigerator. Wednesday: make cornbread, cook giblets, boil eggs, chop onion and celery. Thursday morning: assemble and bake.

name: Coconut Fruit Smoothies
ingredients: 1/2c fruit of choice (bananas, berries, mango, peaches)
sugar or honey to taste, or 1/3c protein powder
instructions: Add coconut milk, orange juice, ice, fruit, and sweetener or protein powder to blender. Blend until smooth and serve.
notes: Makes 2 large smoothies. From A Taste of Thai.

name: Coconut Pancakes
instructions: Sift flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt into large bowl. Mix in flaked coconut. Beat coconut milk, eggs, oil, and extract together. Make a well in the middle of flour and pour in liquid ingredients. Mix just until combined. Pour slightly less than 1/2 cup batter onto lightly greased and preheated griddle (375°F). Cook until small bubbles appear and flip. Cook until golden.
notes: Makes 12 large pancakes. From A Taste of Thai.

name: Coconut Custard Pie
ingredients: 1 9-inch homemade or frozen pie crust, unbaked
instructions:
Preheat oven to 400°F. If using frozen pie crust thaw 15 minutes. Line crust with parchment paper, fill with uncooked rice or beans and bake 12 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Reduce oven to 350°F.

Add eggs, sugar, vanilla, and salt to mixing bowl and beat well. Whisk 1/4 cup of the coconut milk with cornstarch in a saucepan until cornstarch is dissolved. Stirring constantly over medium heat (do not boil) add remaining coconut milk. Cook until it begins to thicken. Remove from heat. Whisking constantly, slowly drizzle hot coconut milk into egg mixture. Pour mixture into pre-baked pie shell. Sprinkle with coconut. Bake 35-45 minutes until custard is firmly set. Cool on wire rack. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Grandma Beck's Sweet Potato Casserole
ingredients: 1 pint whipping cream (less 2T — save for butter)
instructions: Heat potatoes with their liquid over medium-high heat until bubbling hot. Drain. Add butter. When butter is melted, mash potatoes with electric mixer. Add cream and beat until well-mixed. Turn into greased casserole and smooth top. Sprinkle with chopped pecans if desired. Cover and bake at 350° about 30 minutes. Uncover and top with marshmallows spaced about 1/2 inch apart. Bake 15 more minutes until marshmallows are puffed and lightly browned.
notes: Thanksgiving family recipe from Grandma Beck.

name: Southern Green Beans
ingredients: 3 lbs frozen or fresh-cut green beans
instructions:
Store-bought frozen: Melt butter in large skillet with a lid. Add beans (remove from freezer about 45 minutes ahead of time for easier handling). Sprinkle with salt. Cover and cook over low heat, just enough to make them sizzle, about 1 hour, stirring 2 or 3 times.

Canned variation: Use 3 cans Libby's Shellie Green Beans and 6T bacon grease instead. Drain liquid from beans into a pot, add bacon grease, cook over medium heat until grease melts. Add beans. Continue cooking until heated through, about 15 minutes.
notes: Thanksgiving family recipe. Three methods: fresh (skip it!), frozen with butter, or canned with bacon grease.

name: Orange and Raspberry Tart
ingredients: juice of one orange plus enough water to make 1/3 cup
~2 cups fresh raspberries or other berries
instructions:
Preheat oven to 350°. In a medium bowl sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon. Whisk dry ingredients together and set aside. In another bowl whisk together the egg and sugar vigorously until mixture is pale yellow, about 1 minute. Whisk in the oil, extract, zest, and juice mixture until well-blended. Scrape the wet ingredients into the dry with a rubber spatula and stir gently until combined — do not overmix.

Line the bottom of an 8-inch pie pan with raised center with parchment paper and spray with nonstick spray. Pour the batter in and bake until center springs back when gently pressed, about 25-30 minutes. Let cool 15 minutes before unmolding, then chill in freezer 15 minutes to cool completely.

Meanwhile place orange marmalade and boiling water in a bowl and whisk until jam is loosened. Add berries and stir to coat. Flip the cooled cake so the concave side is up. Poke holes in the bottom with a toothpick or fork. Spoon the raspberry mixture onto the cake and arrange berries. Dust with powdered sugar before serving if desired.
notes: Serves 8. Start to finish 1 hour including baking and cooling.

name: Lemon Poppy Seed Muffins
ingredients: 1/4 cup (60g) sour cream or full fat Greek yogurt, room temperature
1/4 cup (60g) fresh lemon juice for syrup
lemon peel from 1 lemon for syrup
instructions:
In a large bowl whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and poppy seeds. In another bowl mix together melted butter, oil, eggs, sour cream, vanilla, lemon zest, lemon juice, and milk. Pour the wet mixture into the dry and use a rubber spatula to combine. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and rest at room temperature for 1 hour.

Meanwhile make the lemon simple syrup: add lemon juice and sugar to a saucepan, bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes until sugar dissolves. Peel zest from 1 lemon and add to bowl. Remove syrup from heat and pour into the bowl of zest. Cool at room temperature.

Close to the 1 hour mark preheat oven to 425°F and line a muffin tin with 11 paper liners. Using a large 2oz scoop (about 1/4 cup) fill each liner all the way to the top. Bake for 8 minutes, then change oven heat to 350°F and bake another 8-10 minutes until toothpick comes out clean with a few moist crumbs. Brush warm muffins with a generous amount of lemon simple syrup. Cool in pan 5 minutes then transfer to rack. Sprinkle with more poppy seeds if desired. Best served still warm.
notes: Makes 11 muffins. By Jenna Barnard at Butternut Bakery. Printed 3/24/26.

name: Easy Kalakand
ingredients: 15 oz ricotta cheese, full fat (Sorrento or Calabro recommended)
14 oz condensed milk, full fat (Eagle, Carnation, or Magnolia recommended)
instructions: Line a small baking tray or dish with 7"x7" parchment paper. In a wide non-stick pan (10-11 inches) add ricotta cheese and condensed milk. Cook over medium heat stirring frequently for 20-25 minutes, scraping the sides frequently. In the first 5 minutes the mixture will be very liquidy and will continue to thicken. After about 20 minutes the mixture will start to separate from the sides and come together as a thickish batter. Add cardamom and mix well. Pour into the parchment-lined dish and using a silicone spatula press down evenly making a 6"x6" square, evening out the top and sides. Sprinkle pistachios and saffron on top and gently press down. Allow to cool completely, about 1 hour. Cut into 1 inch cubes (about 36 pieces) or 2"x2" squares (9 pieces). Store at room temperature up to 1 day, refrigerate up to 5 days. Freezes well — thaw overnight in fridge and serve at room temperature.
notes: Serves 9. Indian ricotta cheese sweet (milk cake). 4.91/5 from 61 votes. By Archana Mundhe.

name: Easy Homemade Caramel Corn
instructions: Pop popcorn and remove all unpopped kernels. Salt the popcorn — sweet and salty goes great with caramel. Melt butter in a medium saucepan over low/medium heat. Add brown sugar and stir until thoroughly mixed. If you see a thin layer of butter on the surface continue to stir on low heat until completely combined. Increase heat to medium-low, just enough to bring the caramel to a low boil. When surface starts to bubble set a timer for 4 minutes and stop stirring. After 4 minutes remove from heat and stir in vanilla and baking soda (mixture will foam). Pour over popcorn immediately and stir to coat. Spread on parchment-lined baking sheet and allow to cool about 5 minutes.
notes: Yields 10 cups. Total time 25 minutes. No corn syrup needed.

name: Chess Cake
instructions:
First layer: Mix together cake mix, melted butter, and beaten eggs until well combined. Spread over bottom of greased 9x13 pan.

Second layer: Beat cream cheese, powdered sugar, eggs, and melted butter together with electric mixer until thoroughly combined. Spread over first layer.

Bake at 350° (325° for glass pan) for 1 hour until golden brown. Cake will fall when taken from oven — this is normal.
notes: Judy McKenzie's recipe. Called the next best thing to a butter roll.

name: Whipped Butter
ingredients: 2 sticks butter, softened at room temperature
instructions: Beat softened butter for several minutes with electric mixer until fluffy. Beat in whipping cream.
notes: Thanksgiving family recipe. Serve with raised rolls.

name: Apple Butter French Toast Bake
ingredients: brioche loaf (~16 oz), cut into 1-inch cubes
powdered sugar and maple syrup for topping
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F and grease a baking dish. Brown the butter and whisk with apple butter. Then whisk in eggs, cream, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt. Add cubed brioche to dish. Pour mixture over and gently toss to coat. Bake 45 minutes until set. Dust with powdered sugar, drizzle with maple syrup, and serve warm.
notes: From Vital Farms. Uses Vital Farms salted butter and eggs.

name: Grandma Beck's Crispy Crunch
instructions: Put brown sugar, corn syrup, and butter in a saucepan. Cook on medium heat stirring constantly until it begins to boil. Cook 90 seconds more. Spray two 9x13 inch pans with nonstick spray. Put half of both the cereal and peanuts in each pan. Pour the hot mixture over the cereal and gently stir to evenly coat. Bake at 325° for 7 minutes. Take out and gently stir. Return to oven and bake an additional 7 minutes. Line 3 cookie sheets with parchment paper and pour the cereal mixture out onto them. Let cool completely. After well cooled, add Peanut M&Ms if desired.
notes: Grandma Beck's recipe #1. "To be important in the eyes of a child is to be truly important."

name: Southern Sweet Potato Casserole
instructions:
Combine sweet potatoes, sugar, eggs, vanilla, milk, and butter. Beat with electric mixer until smooth. Spoon into greased 2-qt shallow casserole.

For topping: combine brown sugar, flour, butter, and pecan meal. Sprinkle over top of potatoes. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes.
notes: Serves 8. From the kitchen of Cathleen Waites.

name: Toll House Cupcakes
instructions:
Combine butter, sugars, and vanilla. Beat until creamy. Beat in egg. Sift remaining dry ingredients together and stir into sugar mixture. Spoon into prepared cups dividing evenly. Bake 375° for 12 minutes.

Topping: Beat together brown sugar, egg, and salt until thick. Add chocolate chips, chopped walnuts, and vanilla. Spoon onto top of each cupcake. Bake 15 more minutes.
notes: Makes 16. From the kitchen of Cathleen Waites.

name: Chex Muddy Buddies
ingredients: 9 cups Rice Chex, Corn Chex, Chocolate Chex, or Peanut Butter Chex (or combination)
instructions: Measure cereal into large bowl and set aside. In 1-quart microwavable bowl, microwave chocolate chips, peanut butter, and butter uncovered on High 1 minute. Stir. Microwave about 30 seconds longer or until mixture can be stirred smooth. Stir in vanilla. Pour mixture over cereal, stirring until evenly coated. Pour into 2-gallon resealable food-storage plastic bag. Add powdered sugar. Seal bag and shake until well coated.
notes: Makes 18 servings (1/2 cup each). Ready in 15 minutes. From Chex cereal box.
